content: The Health and Wellbeing Directorate is a division of the Scottish Government. It holds responsibility for overseeing the Scottish National Health Service (NHS) and for formulating and implementing policies related to health and community care services. This directorate was originally established in 1999 under the name Scottish Executive Health Department and underwent a renaming in 2007. The Cabinet Secretary for Health and Wellbeing is Nicola Sturgeon, who is supported in her role by the Minister for Public Health, Shona Robison. The department operates under the leadership of a Director-General, who is supported by a Chief Medical Officer.
